1.note: In Exod 22:8 הָאֱלֹהִים is traditionally read as "the judges"; here it stands for the judge the two men come to.

2.note: Gen 38:14, where Tamar sits at Petaḥ-Enaim ("the opening of the eyes", or of the springs) to wait for Judah. The ant sits at the opening of her hole by the road.

3.note: זֶרַע is both "seed" (grain) and "offspring": the ant has no grain in her house, as a widow has no child.

4.note: Exod 22:1 "if the thief is found breaking in (בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת)". מַחְתֶּרֶת is also a tunnel: the ant is found in her burrow.

5.note: Exod 12:17 "you shall guard the matzot". "Guarded matzah" (מַצָּה שְׁמוּרָה) is wheat watched from the harvest so that it does not become leaven; the ant's wheat is guarded in the same way.

6.he: וְתִגְלֶה מִמְּעוֹנָהּ רַק / לְבֵית לֶחֶם מְמַהֶרֶת
6.note: תִּגְלֶה is "goes into exile" and also "comes into the open". Bethlehem (בֵּית לֶחֶם) is read as "the house of bread": she leaves her hole only to hurry to food. The next line goes on with the idea of exile.

7.note: הֲמָסִים follows Isa 64:1 כִּקְדֹחַ אֵשׁ הֲמָסִים, usually "brushwood" (a word found only there). The sense of the line is uncertain.

8.he: לֶחֶם רֶשַׁע יִלְחַם. וּבְלִי שֶׁלַח יִלְחַם
8.note: The two lines end with the same word יִלְחַם, "he eats" (from לֶחֶם, bread) and "he fights".

9.note: Gen 32:3, Jacob names the place Maḥanaim, "two camps". The dual form fits the place between the two breasts.

10.note: Gen 39:17, Potiphar's wife: "the Hebrew slave came in to me". Here "Hebrew" is changed to "Cushite", the black flea.

11.note: מַצֵּבָה is a pillar or a standing place; the word seems chosen for the rhyme with קֵבָה. The sense is uncertain.

12.note: The subject is uncertain: the flea picks the red "lily" (the blood) before it blooms, or one picks off the flea before he grows.

13.he: יְקַצֵּר אֶת תְּנוּמָתִי וְאַךְ יַ־ / אֲרִיךְ לֵילִי וְשָׂם רֹאשׁוֹ בְּסוֹפוֹ
13.note: The Hebrew splits the word יַאֲרִיךְ ("he lengthens") across the two half-lines; the English does the same. "Sets its head at its end" seems to mean that the night has no end: its start is joined to its close.

14.he: וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֶחְבִּיר הָאֵל הַמְּלִיצוֹת בֵּינֵיכֶם. הִתְחַבְּרוּ בִידִידוּת שְׁנֵיכֶם
14.note: הֶחְבִּיר and הִתְחַבְּרוּ ("joined", "be joined") play on the name חֶבֶר (Ḥever), which the old man reveals at the end.
